_meta.note: Two jurisdictions apply at once. China taxes the source event; the United States taxes the person on worldwide income. The transfer itself is not a third tax.

rows.rule: Domiciled in China, or resident 183 days or more in a tax year
rows.amount: Residency determines whether worldwide or China-source income is taxed
rows.note: A U.S. citizen working in China can be a Chinese tax resident and a U.S. taxpayer at the same time.
Withheld by the employer; conversion later does not add wage tax.
Gain = proceeds minus original value, taxes paid and reasonable costs.

rows.rule: Full 3% if held under 2 years; exempt at 2 years or more
Self-used 5+ years and only family home
rows.note: Requires a signed undertaking plus family and housing evidence.

rows.topic: FIE dividends to a foreign individual
rows.note: The 1994 exemption is repealed. Treaty relief is possible but fact-specific.

rows.rule: No inheritance-tax statute located in this session
rows.note: The transfer still requires SAFE approval and tax clearance for the estate's assets.

rows.rule: Citizens are taxed on income from all sources
rows.note: Citizenship, not residence, drives the filing duty.

rows.rule: Section 988 ordinary gain on disposition of nonfunctional currency
rows.amount: Ordinary rates on the rate-driven gain
rows.note: Needs a USD basis per tranche of RMB.

rows.rule: Credit for foreign income taxes paid or accrued, subject to limitation
rows.note: Claimed on Form 1116; the limitation can leave a residual U.S. tax.

rows.rule: 1984 convention limits source-country tax on dividends, interest and royalties to 10%
rows.note: The saving clause preserves U.S. taxation of citizens. Article 12 (Gains) must be read before relying on treaty relief.

rows.rule: Form 3520 if more than USD 100,000 from a nonresident alien or foreign estate
FBAR above USD 10,000 aggregate; Form 8938 above the applicable threshold
rows.note: Neither depends on the account producing income.
No state of residence was supplied.

ordering: Tax attaches to the event, not to the wire.
China taxes first at the source event: wages 3-45%, asset gains 20%, dividends 20%.
The U.S. then taxes the person on worldwide income; the foreign tax credit reduces double taxation but is limited.
Section 988 can add ordinary income purely from RMB appreciation, even when the principal was already taxed.
Reporting penalties (FBAR, 8938, 3520) are fixed-dollar exposures that have nothing to do with the amount converted.
